title: Adapt only among declared valid strategies

facts.note: Task text mentions choosing between strategies from workload/resource signals.

values: work selects among two or more declared strategies using workload or resource signals (including handling when those signals are absent)
facts.note: Whether a plan, acceptance, doc, implementation or review concerns signal-driven strategy selection requires reading its content; applies in any phase.

fires: A plan, wagon or WMBT proposes choosing between already declared strategies based on measured workload size or resource availability.
An acceptance or doc describes how to select among declared strategies from workload or resource signals, e.g. its thresholds, fallback or behavior when those signals are missing.
Implementation or review work on an existing signal-driven selection among declared strategies.
doesNotFire: Work uses a single fixed strategy with no signal-driven selection.
Work that does not involve choosing between strategies at all.
A selection policy with thresholds or fallback that does not choose among strategies using workload or resource signals.

given: Work involves selecting among two or more already declared valid strategies based on workload or resource signals, whether those signals are present or missing
when: planning, specifying, implementing or reviewing that selection
then: Choose only among the declared strategies via a deterministic, inspectable selection policy with a stable fallback, preserving accepted outputs and route obligations.
prefer: Use adaptive selection only where measured workload variation justifies multiple strategies and switching overhead.
Acceptances testing thresholds, missing metrics, fallback, oscillation and equivalence across workload classes; benchmark total cost.
Interlocking guards selecting between deterministic alternatives.
avoid: Suppressing failure behavior when signals are absent.
Inferring unimplemented orchestration (e.g. dynamic rescheduling) from this pattern; it needs new validated capabilities.
Treating this as enforcement or a new runtime dispatch option; it is advisory guidance and existing plan and source validators still apply.
why: Multiple strategies are only worth their switching overhead where measured workload variation justifies them, and selection must keep accepted outputs and route obligations intact.
evidence: Selection chooses only among already declared valid strategies; no undeclared route or strategy is introduced.
The selection policy (thresholds) is deterministic and inspectable, with a stable fallback, and failure behavior is not suppressed when signals are absent.
Tests/acceptances cover thresholds, missing metrics, fallback, oscillation and equivalence across workload classes, plus a total-cost benchmark.
Existing plan and source validators pass; no unimplemented orchestration capability is relied on.
verifier_detail: Advisory guidance for agents (severity 3), not independent enforcement and not a new runtime dispatch option; existing plan and source validators apply.
Runtime boundary: interlocking guards support deterministic alternatives; dynamic rescheduling requires new validated capabilities.

additions.justification: Source has no explicit activation; derived from the statement and applicability term, covering all phases (planning, implementation, review) since the source does not restrict phase, and including missing-signal situations because the constraints and evidence terms address them.
